title: Paul Graham on startups: ambition, formidable founders, shipping speed and AI
summary: In a short YC interview, Paul Graham argues that starting a startup is essentially unchanged despite AI. Founder quality (being "formidable", driven by fear of failure) and shipping speed still decide outcomes, and you can still start on little money by hitting milestones that unlock the next round.

principles.text: Formidable means getting what you want in any situation; it aligns investor and founder interests.
principles.quote: I think that it's someone who who gets what they want. That's that's the test, right? Do you get what you want?

principles.text: The next giant company comes from the right founders, not a particular idea; founders look the same as 20 years ago.
principles.quote: The answer to your question of where the next giant company comes from is it comes from the right founders, right? It's not some particular idea.

principles.text: Day to day, founders are driven by fear of failure, not by dreams of becoming billionaires.
principles.quote: You know what actually motivates founders dayto-day? The fear of failure.

principles.text: A startup is no credential or easy major; pursue it only if you can endure years of brutal hardness.
principles.quote: With startups, there's no easy major, right? It's like applying to Harvard and being forced to study theoretical physics, right?

principles.text: You can still start on little money: do what you can with what you have and hit a milestone that convinces investors to fund the next stage.
principles.quote: So, you just do what you can on the money you got. As long as you can get to some kind of milestone, then you can convince investors to give you more.

principles.text: AI hasn't changed startup fundamentals; shipping speed still varies and many startups don't ship fast enough.
principles.quote: Everyone always asks me like with all this AI, is anything still the same? And the answer is so far almost everything is exactly the same.
